newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia adopts nine-month draft budget.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia adopts nine-month draft budget.

text.p: Slovenia's government on Thursday adopted a draft budget for the first nine months of 1997, setting government spending at 532.1 billion tolars ($3.4 billion) and income at 505.4 billion.
"We adopted the draft budget because the final one has not been determined yet," Andrej Engelman, state secretary at the ministry of finance, told a news conference.
He said the expected deficit of 26.7 billion tolars would be covered by loans and the 1996 surplus.
In 1996, Slovenia budgeted to spend 594.2 billion tolars on budget income of 599.2 billion.
"If spending would continue with its current pace until the end of the year the budget for the whole year would amount to 780 billion tolars, leaving practically no deficit," Engelman said.

He said the government was expected to send the final 1997 budget proposal to parliament in the middle of July, adding the proposal would most likely include the 1998 budget as well. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439 ($ = 156.3 Slovenian Tolars)
